metadata.title: HSBC Quantum Fraud - Master Scientific Evidence Ledger

claims.claim_statement: Incumbent classical LightGBM baseline calibrated with isotonic regression provides a reproducible starting point.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Established baseline on temporal synthetic split: AUPRC=0.3040, ROC-AUC=0.4833.
claims.limitations: Measured exclusively on synthetic smoke fixture due to external Kaggle/IEEE-CIS credential blocker.

claims.claim_statement: Performance comparison of Quantum Expert vs matched Classical RBF Expert at 0.5% escalation budget.
claims.scientific_conclusion: At 0.5% budget, Quantum Expert AUPRC=0.3041 vs Classical RBF=0.3036 (Δ=+0.0005, 95% CI [-0.0005, +0.0023], p=0.6880). Statistically indistinguishable from null hypothesis (Δ=0 in 95% CI).
claims.limitations: Tested on 2-qubit simulation on synthetic benchmark; classical RBF control tuned on training fold.

claims.claim_statement: Independent audit of uncertainty escalation router: leakage verification and enrichment over random routing.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Router temporal leakage: NONE (Verified). Uncertainty correlates with borderline decisions (Spearman rho=0.0384). At 5% budget, router achieves 1.07x enrichment over base fraud rate.
claims.limitations: Routing effectiveness is bounded by classical base calibration quality.

claims.claim_statement: Chronological vs Random IID splitting performance comparison.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Random IID splitting artificially inflates test AUPRC by +0.0131 relative to strict chronological splitting, proving that temporal validation is mandatory to prevent false optimism.

claims.claim_statement: Positive Semi-Definiteness and geometric spectral health of Quantum Gram matrices.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Quantum Gram matrix is strictly Positive Semi-Definite (0 negative eigenvalues). Effective rank: Quantum Fidelity=5.81, Projected Quantum=5.13, Classical RBF=10.51.
claims.limitations: Computed on N=100 samples with 2-qubit AngleEmbedding + BasicEntanglerLayers.
